newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FREESTYLE SKIING-AUSTRALIANS LAND ON PODIUM.
newsitem.headline: FREESTYLE SKIING-AUSTRALIANS LAND ON PODIUM.

text.p: World champion Kirstie Marshall led an Australian one-two at a freestyle skiing World Cup women's aerials competition on Sunday.

Marshall, who became the first Australian to win a winter sport world championship title with her victory last month in Japan, claimed her third World Cup win of the season with a two-jump combined score of 179.45.
Her compatriot Jacqui Cooper landed a place on the podium for the first time, finishing second with a mark of 174.66.
Canada's Veronica Brenner was third with 172.87, strengthening her lead in the overall standings.
"I had a crash last week and was pretty shaken up but I just made up my mind to go for it today," Marshall said.
American Eric Bergoust won the men's competition with a score of 235.84.
Switzerland's Andy Messerli was second with 226.66 and Jean-Damlen Climonet of France third with 223.82.
